summary: A 98-second, eight-shot storyboard with definitions before use, two distinct saddle attachments, and a five-second final Morse-relation tableau.
content:
GLOBAL DIRECTION
1920×1080, 60fps, silent, Manim CE 0.20.1 Cairo. Midnight #071426; included surface teal #21CDBA with cyan mesh #75E8FF; excluded surface dim blue mesh; scanning plane and boundary gold #FFC766; extrema coral #FF8078; saddles violet #B58AFF. Brightness encodes surface inclusion, never liquid volume. Plane opacity ≤0.08; emphasize its perimeter and actual intersection curves.

Reserve screen y=0–170 px for one main MathTex formula and y=900–1080 px for at most two short caption lines. Geometry stays within the central stage; close-ups may crop the torus but never occupy overlay bands. Use opaque midnight backing for fixed overlays, 48–56 px formula height and ≥34 px captions. All labels are fixed-screen, never behind surfaces. Crossfade formulas sequentially; no accumulated text. Camera angles below are degrees, gamma=0; transitions are continuous and included in shot durations.

VERIFIED GEOMETRY CONTRACT
Use T(u,v)=((2+0.8 cos v)cos u,0.8 sin v,(2+0.8 cos v)sin u), h=z. Orthogonal tangent lengths are 2+0.8 cos v>0 and 0.8. Criticality forces cos u=0 and sin v=0: exactly four isolated points. In rising order, heights are −2.8,−1.2,1.2,2.8; Hessian diagonals are (2.8,0.8),(1.2,−0.8),(−1.2,0.8),(−2.8,−0.8), giving indices 0,1,1,2. This calculation guides implementation; it is not another on-screen slide.

1 — ORIENTATION / 0–7 s
Reveal the upright torus from darkness. Camera (phi,theta,zoom)=(78,−115,0.80) orbits to (76,−70,0.85), exposing tube depth while preserving the central opening. Top MathTex: T^2\colon\ \text{the torus surface}. Bottom: “Topology: properties unchanged by continuous deformation” / “without cutting or gluing.” A brief cyan mesh sweep traces the skin. Purpose: establish that the mathematical object is a surface and explain topology before naming surface types. Fade the definition, retain geometry.

2 — DEFINE THE SWEEP / 7–16 s
Hold the camera. Gold plane enters at a=−3.2 and rises only to −3.0. First show h(x,y,z)=z for three seconds beside a simple vertical height guide; then replace it with M_a=\{p\in T^2:h(p)\le a\}. Caption: “Include surface points at or below height a.” Test membership visibly: the torus remains dim because no points qualify. Finish with “A surface subset—not a liquid volume.” No teal patch appears below the minimum. This establishes the operation before demonstrating its consequences.

3 — DEFINE CRITICALITY AND INDEX; FIRST DISK / 16–34 s
Keep a=−3.0 until definitions finish. Push toward the bottom point: (78,−78,1.10), frame_center=(0,0,−1.8). At 16–21 s show dh_p=0 and caption “Critical point: height has zero derivative in every tangent direction.” Trace two perpendicular surface arcs through the coral minimum; both have horizontal tangent there.
At 21–25 s replace with \det H_p\ne0. Caption: “H is the matrix of second derivatives” / “Morse: every critical point is nondegenerate.”
At 25–30 s replace with \operatorname{index}(p)=\#\{\text{negative eigenvalues of }H_p\}. Caption: “Count independent downward-bending directions.” Animate both arcs bending upward; then show “Minimum: index 0.”
At 30–34 s cross −2.8 and settle at −2.4. A coral point expands into teal skin. Replace the formula with a=-2.4; caption “Disk · one boundary curve.” Trace its single gold rim once. Definitions now precede every attachment.

4 — FIRST SADDLE / 34–50 s
Pull back to (76,−65,0.85), center origin; rise toward −1.2. Before crossing, caption “Morse attachment theorem: topology stays unchanged between critical levels.” Then push to (80,−62,1.18), center=(0,0,−1.2). At the violet saddle, trace T(u_c+t,v_c) and T(u_c,v_c+t), |t|≤0.35: one rises, one descends. Top: \text{saddle: index }1.
Slow the sweep through −1.2. Highlight the new band joining two arcs of the same existing boundary. Caption: “Crossing this saddle attaches a band.” Continue to a=0; restore zoom 0.85. Caption becomes “Cylinder (annulus) · two boundary curves.” Pulse each gold loop separately. The surface remains connected; the band creates the annulus.

5 — SECOND SADDLE / 50–66 s
Orbit to (74,−110,0.85) during the regular rise, then approach (80,−108,1.18), center=(0,0,1.2). Again display \text{saddle: index }1; show opposite curvature directions on the actual torus. Slow through +1.2. Violet emphasis follows a band joining the TWO different boundary curves; visibly merge them into one. Caption: “This band joins the two boundary curves.” Pull back and settle at a=2.4. Caption: “Punctured torus · one boundary curve,” then “A torus with one open disk removed.” Finish: “Disk and punctured torus: same boundary count, different topology.” Never show a stable surface-type label at the singular crossing.

6 — CAP / 66–76 s
Move to (76,−72,0.95), center=(0,0,0.3). Approach the coral maximum. Two surface arcs bend downward; top: \text{maximum: index }2. Raise a through 2.8 to 3.0. Gold boundary contracts to a point and disappears as teal closes the cap. Caption: “Closed torus · no boundary.” Fade the scanning plane; restore center origin and zoom 0.85.

7 — DEFINE EULER CHARACTERISTIC / 76–88 s
Shift the torus slightly right and reduce zoom to 0.72, opening central-stage space for a triangular disk. Top: \chi=V-E+F. Caption: “Euler characteristic counts vertices − edges + faces.” Illuminate three vertices, three edges, one face in that order. Replace the formula with 3-3+1=1. Subdivide one edge and the face; show 4-5+2=1. Caption: “Subdivision preserves the count.” Then show \Delta\chi=(-1)^k with “Morse attachment theorem: an index-k attachment contributes this amount.” Disk, band, band, cap silhouettes pulse sequentially with +1,−1,−1,+1. Explicit theorem attribution makes the animation an illustration, not a claimed proof.

8 — SUMMARY TABLEAU / 88–98 s
Remove the counting inset. Center the complete torus at (76,−75,0.85). Four critical markers return; a narrow side rail aligns their heights with indices 0,1,1,2. At 88–93 s top: m_k=\#\{\text{critical points of index }k\}. Bottom: “disk → cylinder → punctured torus → closed torus.” At 93 s replace the top with \chi(T^2)=m_0-m_1+m_2=1-2+1=0. Remove the side rail and bottom caption; hold the entire luminous torus and formula motionless for five seconds.

IMPLEMENTATION HANDOFF
Use the approved analytic sublevel parametrization and exact cross-section branches, including saddle figure-eights and endpoint identifications. Use ≤48×32 reusable surface patches, sparse mesh curves, and about 192 samples per boundary branch. Update existing points; avoid rebuilding Surface objects each frame. Use set_camera_orientation, move_camera, and add_fixed_in_frame_mobjects. Required downstream video review: overlay clearance, depth ordering, continuous reconnections, readable holds, and absence of false seam boundaries.
checks: Read both approved upstream artifacts and repaired definition order explicitly.
Independently recomputed critical heights, Hessian determinants and indices in JavaScript: determinants 2.24, −0.96, −0.96, 2.24; maximum gradient residual 5.144×10⁻¹⁶.
Attempted the requested Python interpreter; execution failed with Access is denied. Inspected installed Manim source directly for camera, fixed-overlay and Surface APIs.
Eight contiguous shots total 98 seconds; the final formula holds for five seconds. Surface labels occur at regular levels.
No files edited, no delegation, and no render performed. Primary theorem references are inherited from the approved mathematics dossier, not newly retrieved.
sources: John Milnor, Morse Theory, §§2–3 and §6, as documented in mathematics.json: https://math.stanford.edu/~ralph/math215b/Milnor.pdf
